name: Jumping Through Segments
description: Polycarp is designing a level for a game. The level consists of $$$n$$$ segments on the number line, where the $$$i$$$-th segment starts at the point with coordinate $$$l_i$$$ and ends at the point with coordinate $$$r_i$$$. The player starts the level at the point with coordinate $$$0$$$. In one move, they can move to any point that is within a distance of no more than $$$k$$$. After their $$$i$$$-th move, the player must land within the $$$i$$$-th segment, that is, at a coordinate $$$x$$$ such that $$$l_i \le x \le r_i$$$. This means: After the first move, they must be inside the first segment (from $$$l_1$$$ to $$$r_1$$$); After the second move, they must be inside the second segment (from $$$l_2$$$ to $$$r_2$$$); ... After the $$$n$$$-th move, they must be inside the $$$n$$$-th segment (from $$$l_n$$$ to $$$r_n$$$). The level is considered completed if the player reaches the $$$n$$$-th segment, following the rules described above. After some thought, Polycarp realized that it is impossible to complete the level with some values of $$$k$$$. Polycarp does not want the level to be too easy, so he asks you to determine the minimum integer $$$k$$$ with which it is possible to complete the level.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)—the number of test cases. Descriptions of the test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)—the number of segments in the level. The following $$$n$$$ lines. The $$$i$$$-th line contain two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$0 \le l_i \le r_i \le 10^9$$$)—the boundaries of the $$$i$$$-th segment. Segments may intersect. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer—the minimum value of $$$k$$$ with which it is possible to complete the level.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1907D — Jumping Through Segments [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
